tech.title: Handing over humanity

This might not be such a desirable outcome, as humans have a natural desire for freedom. The arrangement will probably not work, as keeping power responsive to human needs has required checks developed over centuries, sustained by repeated feedback from the real world and correction, and there's no reason to keep that equilibrium stable once humans have surrendered all control. Humans have the ability now to steer the technology in a way that will not lead to a complete replacement of human judgment.

webdev.title: What Is Eval-Driven Development? How to Improve AI Agents
webdev.summary: Tweaking agents by hand-testing a few prompts makes it hard to tell whether a change helped or hurt, since outputs vary and several answers can be correct. LangChain proposes a test-driven-style loop: write a pass/fail spec for one behavior, build the dataset and evaluator before the change, then compare experiments example by example, since a higher average can hide regressions. It also urges keeping a held-out set to catch overfitting and running evals in CI and on live traffic, feeding production failures back into the dataset.

webdev.title: How we cut Next.js memory from ~5GB to ~1GB: the react-query timer holding every SSR request
webdev.summary: Zepto's Next.js pods sat at about 5 GB because react-query v3 starts a multi-minute cache timer for every query rendered on the server, and Node ties each timer to the request's AsyncLocalStorage context, keeping every finished request in memory. Building server-side queries with an infinite cache time stopped the timers and dropped pods to about 1.2 GB, and the same trap still applies on v5 when hooks set an explicit gcTime. The fix also exposed that autoscaling had been driven by the leak, so teams fixing memory issues should watch replica counts and latency afterward.

webdev.title: My HTML Wishlist: Partial HTML Includes

This essay argues for ordinary HTML pages to opt into exposing specific fragments, while acknowledging parser, buffering, and cross-origin constraints.

data.title: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System

data.title: Parquet's Revised Modular Footer Proposal: Row Groups Stop Being Physical Boundaries
data.summary: A revised Apache Parquet proposal would replace monolithic Thrift footers with independently readable metadata modules encoded as Parquet pages. Column chunks become contiguous page sequences, row-group metadata becomes optional, and statistics can describe arbitrary row ranges rather than fixed groups. Readers could retrieve metadata only for relevant columns, reducing planning overhead on wide tables. The redesign remains under community review and would require changes across readers and writers.

data.title: Iceberg v4 Stats-Only Fields: How Tables Store Statistics for Partition Expressions
data.summary: Apache Iceberg v4 introduces stats-only fields that store metadata for derived expressions, such as partition buckets or case-normalized strings, without materializing additional table columns. Statistics are encoded as typed fields in manifest content_stats structures, enabling expression-aware file pruning. A new file-level tight_stats flag identifies exact live-row counts and eligible bounds, improving planning and potentially enabling metadata-only computations without scanning underlying data files.

data.title: Timestral, t0, Tabby, and Morpheus-2.0 Compared on GIFT-Eval

Closed platforms, by contrast, carry per-seat costs, manual workarounds, and lock-in, which can force a full rebuild when switching vendors.

design.title: Where the Disabled Button Got Its Rule
design.summary: The familiar convention of graying out unavailable controls traces back to Apple's Lisa interface guidelines from 1980, when dimmed menu items could still be selected even though they performed no action. By 1983, Apple had changed the rule so disabled commands could no longer be activated, a behavior later inherited by Macintosh interfaces and HTML's disabled attribute. Comparing eight modern design systems reveals how this convention creates accessibility problems, particularly when disabled buttons cannot receive keyboard focus or explain why an action is unavailable, making focusable alternatives such as aria-disabled useful.

marketing.title: The next big creators will be experts

Four qualities matter when evaluating expert voices: a genuine obsession with their subject, the ability to hold attention beyond short clips, transparency about sources and uncertainty, and the willingness to challenge a brand's assumptions. Pairing experienced experts with younger creators who understand modern formats can also help turn specialized knowledge into content that travels widely.

founders.summary: SaaS renewal prices rise 8-12% annually, with aggressive vendors increasing prices by 15-25%. Vendors like Canva and Microsoft have led with notable price hikes. Canva increased by 317% for its Teams plan. Companies negotiating renewals 90 days in advance save on average 49%, highlighting the importance of early negotiation.

founders.title: 5 GTM plays working right now
founders.summary: Marketers at incident.io can launch the ads and landing page for one target account in three minutes, a job that took their agency two or three days. The Claude workflow behind it already knows the approved messaging and which accounts show buying signals. Clay pointed a similar agent at attribution and found a $200,000 deal credited to a Google ad actually started two months earlier with a free trial.

founders.title: The Growth Meta: How to Build a Sales Pipeline
founders.summary: The playbook for great sales is always evolving. This article looks at how founders are building strong sales pipelines using the latest technology. Founders are now turning sales calls into brainstorming sessions, leading with proof rather than a pitch, and starting enterprise GTM on day one. Founders need to learn to find customers, earn their trust, and get them to pay before they hire a sales team.

founders.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR
founders.summary: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach founders, operators and startup leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities .

founders.title: Gemini Decisions API: Fast, calibrated multimodal decisions
founders.summary: The Gemini Decisions API can evaluate up to 1,000 yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring questions in a fast, single pass. It can accept text, images, audio, video, and PDF input. Powered by Google's new Gemini Decision 1 model, the model is available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio. It costs $0.10 per 2 million tokens - outputs are free.

founders.title: What's new in Grok Bot 1.0
founders.summary: Grok Bot 1.0 adds Team Bots you can publish and share, Slack and Microsoft Teams, meetings on Meet and Zoom, shared connectors, and reviewed learnings. It is now a personal assistant that the whole team can talk to in the app, in Slack, in Microsoft Teams, and in video calls. This post covers how to create a Team Bot and publish it, how to bring the bot into Microsoft Teams, how to add a bot to a meeting, and more. It also looks at the new admin controls and what's possible without a team.

founders.title: Why Should Managers Exist?
founders.summary: AI advancements challenge the necessity of traditional firms by reducing transaction costs for coordination tasks traditionally handled by managers. While AI enables easy execution of tasks like negotiating refunds or coding, its integration into firms introduces coordination complexities. Effective integration depends on the formalization of interfaces and authority concentration, dictating whether AI can support autonomy or if managerial oversight is still required.

founders.title: How to Run Go-to-Market With a 2-Person Team: The AI Agent Stack We Use to Publish, Prospect, and Close
founders.summary: A two-person team can effectively execute a go-to-market strategy using an AI agent stack to handle repetitive tasks, while humans focus on judgment and approvals. This setup allows publishing, prospecting, and closing work to flow efficiently by automating research, enrichment, scoring, and drafting processes. With costs totaling $1,412 monthly, the team achieves a significant return, booking meetings and closing deals that normally require a larger team.

founders.title: AI makes startup branding crucial
founders.summary: Startups face intense competition due to easy LLC formation and AI advancements, making strong branding crucial from day one. Building a brand system, establishing a founder voice, and leveraging creator trust effectively differentiate a startup in this crowded space. Investing in branding early can significantly impact growth and pipeline generation.

founders.title: Company.md: A Fundraising Brief for Investor Agents
founders.summary: Founders are adding company.md files to fundraising materials, consolidating business information into Markdown for investors' AI agents.

founders.title: Flo gets 40% of its subscriptions more than six months after install, and wants to keep it that way
founders.summary: Flo keeps cycle tracking free and gets 40% of its subscriptions more than six months after install, offering paid features as users' needs change.

founders.summary: Ro cut more than $50 million in direct-to-consumer revenue in its 2022 reset because the unit economics were upside down.

founders.title: SciFi Investment Theme: Fintech 3.0
founders.summary: The combination of dramatically lower adoption costs and a step-change in agent-powered software will create an opening for a new generation of B2B Fintech companies to reinvent areas like AP/AR, treasury management, and the broader financial back office.

founders.title: There are basically two kinds of companies to build right now
founders.summary: Companies that get AI diffused very close to where the work is being done, and companies that use AI to accelerate scientific progress, then build products from that progress.

crypto.title: New York federal judge denies Novig's injunction bid
crypto.summary: Judge Colleen McMahon denied the preliminary injunction Novig sought against New York, finding that its sports event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act because they don't depend on events with a financial or economic consequence, and “bear more than a passing resemblance to sports betting.” That lets the state require Novig to get a gambling license or stop listing sports contracts. Novig's operator, Ludlow Exchange, got CFTC contract market designation in June, began serving New York customers in August, and sued Attorney General Letitia James on August 5, arguing federal preemption. The ruling follows a similar denial for Kalshi earlier this year, and lawyer Daniel Wallach says all 10 Second Circuit federal rulings in sports prediction-market cases have favored the states, with state regulators possibly moving to enforcement in state court.

crypto.title: Alta: Airwallex Co-Founder to Build Onchain Finance Infrastructure
crypto.summary: Alta, operated by Nexus Networks, raised to build onchain finance infrastructure spanning cross-border payments, embedded finance, treasury management, and compliance controls. Founder Loong Wang frames the addressable problem as $4T in trapped cash, $1.4T in counterparty risk, and $135B in operational waste in global corporate finance. The treasury product combines FX conversion at settlement with onchain yield through tokenized money market funds, while the compliance layer applies policy controls at the transaction level across all product areas. A fourth vertical targets agentic commerce, building payment rails for AI agents that transact autonomously.

crypto.title: Visa Adds Monad to Stablecoin Settlement Network
crypto.summary: Visa added Monad as a stablecoin settlement option for participating issuers and acquirers, bringing its blockchain settlement network to 10 chains that also include Ethereum, Solana, Base, Polygon, Avalanche, Stellar, Canton, Tempo, and Circle's Arc. The program reached a $20 billion annualized settlement run rate as of September, up 15x year over year, with 225 stablecoin-linked card programs live globally. Monad is building an institutional privacy feature, expected in the coming months, that keeps transaction details confidential from public view while remaining auditable by regulators and sharing liquidity with the public chain. The network's ability to settle on weekends and holidays distinguishes it from traditional card rails, which operate on a five-business-day banking schedule.

crypto.title: Building a Tokenized Securities Venue on Uniswap
crypto.summary: The SEC's September 2026 Innovation Exemption established Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs), a new venue category permitting AMMs on public blockchains to trade tokenized NMS stocks without registering as exchanges or ATSs, with compliant liquidity providers exempt from dealer registration. Uniswap has processed over $20 billion in stock token volume to date, with Robinhood Chain generating $900 million across 130,000 wallets in three months through 40+ SPY-paired pools. TSV compliance requires KYL and KYC identity gating, per-pool disclosures, and price oracles tied to real-world exchanges, all implementable via Uniswap v4 hooks without modifying the core AMM. The exemption will run for five years and targets a $79 trillion US equities market, where AMM settlement is atomic and final compared to the T+1 cycle in traditional clearinghouses.

crypto.title: Is Hyperliquid Losing Its Long-Tail Liquidity Moat?
crypto.summary: Analysis of orderbook data from November 2025 to November 2026 across 38 comparable markets shows Hyperliquid's long-tail dollar depth fell 82%, versus 61% on Binance and 78% on OKX. After controlling for token price declines, the HL-to-Binance depth ratio dropped 57.5% at 5 bps, with $10k execution costs running 5.21 bps on HL versus 2.95 bps on Binance. Wintermute's monopolization of read priority fees and L1 congestion at 25-40k TPS have disadvantaged smaller market makers, pushing them to widen spreads and reduce depth in response to adverse selection risk. The deterioration threatens Hyperliquid's founding differentiation: deep liquidity in long-tail assets was the moat separating it from centralized venues.

crypto.title: DeFi Moats in an AI World
crypto.summary: AI tooling has collapsed the cost of launching DeFi products from six-month, $3M builds to weekend projects, but Multicoin Capital's Spencer Applebaum argues this commoditization strengthens incumbent protocol moats rather than eroding them. Financial moats, including liquidity depth, customer trust, and proprietary risk underwriting, require years to accumulate and sit beyond what AI can replicate from scratch. Multicoin's updated DeFi value-capture framework adds AI agents as the next class of sophisticated users, gravitating toward protocols with the deepest liquidity and most reliable execution at scale rather than those competing on software features or UI. This positions protocols like Uniswap, Aave, and Hyperliquid as primary beneficiaries as DEX market share against CEXs hits all-time highs and institutional adoption of tokenized assets accelerates.

crypto.title: Stock tokens are where stablecoins were in 2023
crypto.summary: DTCC's new tokenization service is the biggest change in markets since paper certificates went away in the 1970s, yet will be mostly unused for a while. The market is tiny (about 0.004% of stocks and ETFs, with $4.6B of tokenized stocks, nearly all wrapped tokens backed by shares at one broker, Alpaca) and is similar to stablecoins in 2023, about 18 months before they took off. There are currently four models: wrapped (xStocks, no shareholder rights), pooled (OKXICE, where 56 of 62 targeted companies opted out), mirrored (DTCC, with 34 securities on Canton and Besu and one Canton transaction so far), and native (Superstate and Figure, which need SEC rule changes). A Warren-led Senate Banking Committee and faster settlement hurting netting are potential headwinds. Banks that sit out tokenization risk buying it later from Robinhood or BlackRock.

crypto.title: Building Networks for Agents
crypto.summary: The intents model used by protocols like UniswapX, where users sign outcome-specified orders and providers compete to fill them, offers a template for agent-to-agent commerce networks that handle complex multi-party preference matching across everyday goods and services. Exchanges that currently require excessive coordination overhead become tractable when each party's agent can programmatically bid and accept offers within pre-authorized limits. Founders building these networks face four concrete design problems: enabling agent discovery of relevant suppliers, verifying supplier performance, pricing preferences that are fuzzy and multidimensional, and preventing fake demand or supply on either side. Crypto and stablecoins serve as the natural settlement layer for machine-to-machine transactions in these markets.

it.summary: Keeping your business secure and audit-ready shouldn't mean more manual work for IT. But employees change roles, devices fall out of compliance, and AI agents introduce new access requirements. When identity, device, and access controls are managed separately, it's harder to keep track of who has access to what and whether that access is still appropriate. JumpCloud brings identity, device management, and access security together, helping IT teams maintain visibility, reduce manual work, and stay prepared for audits as their environments change. That's intelligent, secure IT in action. See what continuous compliance can do for you .

it.title: Working with Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors
it.summary: Anthropic announced new workplace features, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. New interactive connectors allow users to open and work within third-party applications like Adobe, Notion, Atlassian, Salesforce, and HubSpot directly inside the Claude interface.

it.title: Anthropic targets workplace collaboration with Claude Meetings
it.summary: Anthropic has introduced Claude Meetings, Whiteboards, and Sheets, expanding its AI assistant into workplace collaboration and productivity. Claude Meetings can participate in Google Meet calls, take notes, retrieve information, and create action plans during discussions. The meeting feature is in beta for Team and Enterprise customers, bringing Anthropic into closer competition with Microsoft and Google.

it.title: Yandex restores 97% of customer data after drone attacks, the rest is permanently lost
it.summary: Russian cloud provider Yandex recovered approximately 97% of affected customer data following drone strikes on three data centers in October. The remaining 2.84% is permanently lost due to hardware damage and the absence of customer backups. Yandex says it will enable backups by default and expand its infrastructure across additional independent locations.

it.title: Platform engineering needs to become more human…and less
it.summary: The rise of AI agents and non-technical builders requires platform engineering to evolve from serving predictable engineers to supporting a chaotic mix of human improvisers and precise automated agents. To manage this shift safely, platforms must automate unwritten guardrails into machine-readable policies, enforce scoped identities, and adopt control loops inspired by Kubernetes.

it.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
it.summary: Cisco announced that all new products starting in 2027 will integrate with its Cloud Control management platform, providing a unified interface for networking, security, and observability. The service will expand internationally beginning in February, with additional countries following in May. Cisco also plans to simplify ThousandEyes licensing and expand its Live Protect capabilities across more networking products.

it.title: Gartner Research: Only 11% of Organizations Turn AI Ambition Into Real Value
it.summary: Most organizations are increasing AI investment, but very few translate it into measurable business outcomes. Gartner's 2027 CIO Agenda reveals four critical disconnects and the three practices leading organizations use to bridge them. Learn how to govern AI economics, redirect investment, and redesign work .

it.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
it.summary: US data center electricity demand has grown approximately 19% annually since 2000, compared with roughly 2% annual growth in grid capacity, according to an analysis by insurance broker Howden. The firm estimates data centers could need to source as much as 58% of their electricity outside the grid by 2030 to maintain their current share of grid capacity. Power availability, lengthy connection delays, and on-site generation costs are becoming major constraints on AI infrastructure expansion.

it.title: Adobe opens Creative Cloud apps to third-party AI assistants
it.summary: Adobe plans to let AI assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude directly edit content within Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects through Model Context Protocol integrations. The capability is scheduled for private beta in early 2027 and aims to preserve manual editing control while automating repetitive creative tasks. Analysts see the move as part of a broader shift toward AI assistants becoming the primary interface for enterprise applications.

it.title: IBM and Microsoft's Imagine Enterprise Puts Agentic Governance Claims to the Test
it.summary: IBM Consulting and Microsoft have jointly launched Imagine Enterprise, an agentic AI platform targeting regulated industries including financial services, insurance, and retail. The platform combines IBM Consulting's library of over 6,000 prebuilt AI agents with Microsoft's Azure cloud, Entra identity management, Purview data governance, and Defender and Sentinel security tooling. Enterprises using the platform remain responsible for satisfying their own regulatory obligations, even where the platform supplies governance tooling.

it.title: GraphRAG Is the New Way to Hold Knowledge
it.summary: GraphRAG significantly outperforms traditional RAG for business AI applications by storing knowledge as interconnected entities and relationships rather than disconnected text fragments. While GraphRAG offers superior performance on multi-step reasoning and broad summaries, it involves substantially higher indexing and processing costs, though newer lightweight implementations are reducing that overhead.

it.title: ABAP Platform Becoming an Enterprise-Grade Execution Backbone for Agentic AI
it.summary: The ABAP platform is an enterprise-grade execution backbone for agentic AI within the Autonomous Enterprise vision. The role of agents acts as an abstraction layer for outcome-driven interactions and upcoming developments include governance, reliability, scaling, and the ABAP Model Context Protocol server.

it.title: Anthropic signs another $4.3bn in compute agreements with Microsoft
it.summary: Anthropic has expanded its Microsoft cloud computing agreements by up to $4.3 billion as it secures additional infrastructure capacity ahead of its planned IPO.

it.title: 10-year data center moratorium approved in Ottawa, Kansas
it.summary: Nearly 72% of voters supported the restriction.

it.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
it.summary: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears.

it.title: Mozilla Thunderbird email service edges closer to launch with early access
it.summary: Mozilla-backed Thunderbird has begun offering early access to Thundermail, its paid email hosting service featuring custom domains, 30GB of storage, and integration with Thunderbird's desktop and mobile apps.
